messages:
Aisha: heads-up — we saw a new pattern this morning in eu-west: a single tenant on a shared rack started saturating the PCIe fabric and pushed up p95 latency for other tenants by ~3x.
Tom: ugh. any obvious root cause? noisy GPUs or network egress?
Marcos: looked at perf counters — PCIe bandwidth and tail latencies spike when that tenant runs batched generation with long context. NVLink lanes fine, it's PCIe DMA + kernel queueing.
Aisha: tenant is on default shared pool, not dedicated. They bumped batch size after a perf test.
Priya: do we have allocation tags to prefer local-rack affinity for latency-sensitive tenants?
Marcos: we do, but current allocator only honors "rack_affinity" for Dedicated pools. Shared pools ignore it to maximize packing.
Jian: quick thought: could we add a soft-affinity heuristic for requests that declare slo=latency? e.g., try local-rack for the first N placements, fall back after timeout.
Tom: that would reduce noisy neighbor surface but reduces bin-packing. need cost estimate.
Aisha: ran numbers — moving 15% of shared traffic to soft-affinity increases GPU-hours by ~9% in eu-west peak.
Priya: acceptable for customers who pay for latency tier. Can we gate by tenant tag? e.g., tenants with "latency_tier": "premium" get soft affinity.
Marcos: implementation sketch: allocator change + NIC shaping per NIC to cap egress burst for non-premium. Also add eviction hint to scheduler.
Jian: sample allocator change (pseudo):
```
POST /allocate?pool=shared&zone=eu-west-1&tags=latency:premium&soft_affinity=true
{
  "placement_hint": "rack_local",
  "timeout_ms": 200
}
```
Aisha: plus we should add a short-term mitigation: auto-throttle heavy batch sizes when co-located tenants see >1.5x baseline p95. Could be a per-tenant rate-limit.
Tom: ops question — how to roll this without mass migrations? prefer dynamic placement on new requests only.
Marcos: agree. Only apply to new allocations and move when nodes drain for other reasons. Also add an admission-control metric so clients see rejections vs increased latency.
Priya: SLA/product note — we need to document cost bump for latency tier and add an opt-in checkbox in Console.
infra-bot: Deploy plan created: alloc-service#4321; rolling rollout to eu-west allocator instances starting in 2h.
Aisha: who can own the NIC shaping config? Marcos?
Marcos: I can do NIC shaping change. Will test on canary rack (rack-eu3b) and report back in this thread.
Tom: also flag to finance — 9% GPU-hour increase is non-trivial if adoption grows. cc @finance on pricing.
Priya: creating a docs PR after Marcos confirms numbers.
Marcos: canary started — applying egress caps (100 MiB/s) on two nodes. Observing p95 for co-tenants dropping ~30% already.
Aisha: nice. keep the throttles conservative; we want graceful degradation not hard failures.
Jian: one more thing — consider exposing "max_batch_tokens" via API per-tenant so we can prevent runaway batch-size regressions.
Priya: added to product backlog.
Aisha: thanks team. Will wait for Marcos canary results and then we can schedule the allocator rollout. :+1:
